crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Tax Structuring and Planning
children.blurb: Tax structuring and planning within AI accounting covers how businesses arrange entities, transactions, and financing to manage tax obligations across jurisdictions, with attention to transfer pricing, permanent establishment, and tax attributes of AI-related assets.

children.name: Transfer Pricing
children.blurb: Transfer pricing concerns the prices charged between related entities within a multinational group for goods, services, intangibles, and financing.

children.name: Research Credits from Engineering Records
children.blurb: Research credits from engineering records concern the use of technical documentation, version histories, test logs, and design notes to substantiate research and development tax credit claims.

children.name: Sales, Use and Value Added Tax
children.blurb: Sales tax, use tax, and value added tax are transaction taxes levied on goods and services, with sales tax charged at the point of sale, use tax owed on taxable purchases where sales tax was not collected, and VAT applied at each stage of production with credit for input tax.

children.name: Audit Defence and Controversy
children.blurb: Audit defence and controversy covers the work of preparing for, responding to, and resolving disputes with tax authorities over positions that involve AI systems, data, or automated decisions.

sections.body: This field deals with how AI businesses and operations with heavy AI use meet tax rules across countries. It covers how companies structure entities and transactions, how they price dealings between affiliates in different jurisdictions, how they claim research credits from engineering records, how they handle sales, use and value added tax, and how they defend audits. In practice, AI is used to read contracts, invoices, ledgers, and engineering logs at scale, to flag inconsistencies, and to draft workpapers for human review. It also helps model tax positions under different fact patterns and jurisdictions. The work is still accounting and legal work, with AI as a tool for extraction, classification, reconciliation, and document review. This section sits inside The AI Accountant and looks at the tax and jurisdictional side of that work.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts of this field are more mature than others. Sales, use and value added tax work has seen broad automation for data extraction, rate lookup, and return preparation, though rules vary by jurisdiction and product. Transfer pricing remains hard because it depends on comparables, functional analysis, and judgment about risk and intangibles. Research credits from engineering records can be supported by AI that links time, code, and project documentation, but the credit still turns on facts and qualified expenses. Audit defence and controversy work uses AI for document review and timeline building, yet the outcome depends on evidence, disclosure, and the applicable law. The honest limit is that AI can organise and surface information, but it cannot decide a tax position or replace professional judgment, and the site tracks 215 compliance and regulation pages, which shows how much of this area is about rules and process rather than pure calculation.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here fit together as a chain from planning to defence, with Tax Structuring and Planning as the entry point for entity choice, holding structures, and arrangements across borders. Transfer Pricing goes deeper into charges between affiliates and the documentation that supports them. Research Credits from Engineering Records shows how technical records become evidence for credit claims. Sales, Use and Value Added Tax covers transaction taxes on goods, services, and digital offerings. Audit Defence and Controversy is where earlier positions meet tax authority review, disputes, and appeals. A reader would start with structuring for the big picture, move to transfer pricing and credits for specific claims, use indirect tax for transaction level rules, and turn to audit defence when a filing is challenged.
